names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 12 noiembrie.
Read out of saint.gr's line for 12 Νοεμβρίου, «Όσιος Νείλος ο Ασκητής», with the rank word left off.

The heading of the calendar's name link behind its line for 12 ноября ст. ст., «Нил Постник, Синайский, пресвитер, отшельник», with the two grade words left off; both are in `types`. The line itself gives the forename and the epithet alone and in lower case, «Прп. Нила постника»; azbyka.ru capitalises the epithet, «прп. Нила Постника (V)».

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 12. новембар ст. ст., „Преп. Нил Синајски.“ — «Преп.» is the `venerable` grade `types` keeps and comes off, while «Синајски» stays: it is the by-name of the mountain, it stands on the name with no rank noun to govern it, and without it the form would collide with the other Nilus this very day keeps. The Russian form already stored is «Нил Постник, Синайский», with the ascetic grade inside it in the older manner this corpus no longer copies.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 12 ноября ст. ст. — «Прп. Нила постника (V).»
doxologia.ro, calendarul pentru 12 noiembrie — «Sfântul Cuvios Nil Pustnicul»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 12ης Νοεμβρίου — «Όσιος Νείλος ο Ασκητής»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 12 Νοεμβρίου εκάστου έτους», the same day the folder already keeps, and the entry is the same man: the eparch of Constantinople who went to Mount Sinai with his son Theodoulos, whose memory the page puts on 14 January. The page refuses its own century: quoting S. Eustratiades it gives the reign of Theodosius the Great (379 - 395), conjectures Theodosius II (408 - 450) instead, and says that Nikodemos's synaxarion, which puts him under Maurice (582 - 602), has it «οὐχὶ ὀρθῶς», not rightly — adding that if the translation of his bones under the emperor Justin (518 - 527) is true, the synaxarion's information cannot stand. Three readings and the page's own argument against one of them: no `dates` object is proposed, and the disagreement is recorded here. It prints an apolytikion and a kontakion that name him, both taken; the Οἶκος that follows them is not a kind the schema holds. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 25.11.2025 (12. новембар ст. ст.) — „Преп. Нил Синајски.“

attestations.note: The day’s third entry. `dates` UNTOUCHED, AND THIS IS THE DAY’S ONE REAL QUESTION: the entry says «Упокојио се мирно око 450. године у 80. години живота земаљског» — reposed about 450, in the eightieth year of his life — where this folder holds 401–500, «5th century», taken from two calendar lines that print nothing but «(V)». About 450 falls INSIDE that century, so recording it as the death would be narrowing a hundred years to one on the authority of a third book, which is the opposite of what the brief sanctions; the figures are in the life and in this note instead, AND THE AUTHOR MAY WANT THEM IN `dates`. The age would also give a birth about 370, which is not written anywhere. WHAT THE ENTRY ADDS: he was prefect in Constantinople before Sinai, a married man with a son and a daughter, and the withdrawal was AGREED WITH HIS WIFE, she going with the daughter to a women’s monastery in Egypt and he with the son to Sinai; sixty years on the mountain; and one saying of his own. The son is a folder this one already relates to in both directions and the life links him.

hymns.text: Cu curgerile lacrimilor tale ai lucrat pustiul cel neroditor şi cu suspinurile cele dintru adânc ai făcut ostenelile tale însutit roditoare; şi te-ai făcut luminător lumii, strălucind cu minunile, Nil, părintele nostru. Roagă-te lui Hristos Dumnezeu ca să mântuiască sufletele noastre.

source.text: Doxologia — «Troparul Sfântului Cuvios Nil Pustnicul» (a common of a venerable father, with his own name set into it)

english.text: With the streams of thy tears thou didst till the barren desert, and with thy sighing from the depths thou madest thy labours bear fruit a hundredfold; and thou becamest a light to the world, shining with wonders, Nilus our father. Pray thou to Christ God that our souls may be saved.

hymns.text: Ταῖς τῶν δακρύων σου ῥοαῖς, τῆς ἐρήμου τὸ ἄγονον ἐγεώργησας, καὶ τοῖς ἐκ βάθους στεναγμοῖς, εἰς ἑκατὸν τοὺς πόνους ἐκαρποφόρησας, καὶ γέγονας φωστήρ, τῇ οἰκουμένῃ λάμπων τοῖς θαύμασι, Νεῖλε Πατὴρ ἡμῶν, Ὅσιε, Πρέσβευε Χριστῷ τῷ Θεῷ, σωθῆναι τὰς ψυχὰς ἡμῶν.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος πλ. δ’ — the first hymn on the page of «Όσιος Νείλος ο Ασκητής», and it names him.

english.text: With the streams of your tears you tilled the barren desert, and with your groanings from the depths you made your labours bear fruit a hundredfold; and you became a beacon, shining upon the inhabited world with wonders, Nilus our venerable father. Intercede with Christ our God that our souls be saved.

hymns.text: Τὰς φρυγανώδεις τῶν παθῶν τῶν ἐκ τοῦ σώματος, ἐπαναστάσεις τιμητικῶς Νεῖλε Μακάριε, ἐν ἀγρύπνῳ σου συνέκοψας ἱκέσιᾳ. Ἀλλ᾽ ὡς ἔχων παῤῥησίαν πρὸς τὸν Κύριον, ἐκ παντοίων μὲ κινδύνων ἐλευθέρωσον, ἵνα κράζω σοι, Χαίροις Πάτερ παγκόσμιε.

source.text: saint.gr, Κοντάκιον, Ἦχος πλ. δ’, Τῇ ὑπερμάχῳ — on the page of «Όσιος Νείλος ο Ασκητής», and it names him.

english.text: The brushwood risings of the passions that come from the body you cut down, blessed Nilus, by your sleepless entreaty. But having boldness before the Lord, set me free from every kind of danger, that I may cry to you: Rejoice, father of the whole world.

hymns.text: Слез твоих теченьми пустыни безплодное возделал еси,/ и иже из глубины воздыханьми во сто трудов уплодоносил еси,/ и был еси светильник вселенней, сияя чудесы, Ниле, отче наш,// моли Христа Бога спастися душам нашим.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 12 ноября ст. ст. — «Тропарь преподобного Нила»

english.text: With the streams of your tears you tilled the barren desert, and with groanings out of the deep you made your labours bear fruit a hundredfold, and you became a lamp to the whole world, shining with wonders, O Nilus our father. Pray to Christ God that our souls may be saved.

hymns.text: Хврастная страстей яже от телесе востания/ сечительно, Ниле блаженне,/ во бденной твоей ссекл еси молитве,/ но, яко имея дерзновение ко Господу,/ от всяких мя бед свободи, да зову ти:// радуйся, отче всемирный.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 12 ноября ст. ст. — «Кондак преподобного Нила»

english.text: The brushwood of the passions that rise up out of the body you cut clean away, O blessed Nilus, in your vigilant prayer; and since you have boldness before the Lord, set me free from every affliction, that I may cry to you: rejoice, father of all the world.

hymns.text: Божественною любовию возгоревся, всеблаженне,/ оставил еси иже в житии молвы/ и постных селитву в горе стяжа,/ от неямсе, вшед в мрак незаходный,/ приемлеши, яко древле Богоносец, Богоначертанная писмена,/ имиже к Божественней добродетели наставляеми, весело вопием ти:/ радуйся, отче Ниле, постником добротворение.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 12 ноября ст. ст. — «Ин кондак преподобнаго Нила Постника»

english.text: Kindled with the love of God, O all-blessed one, you left behind the clamour of life and won a dwelling of fasters on the mountain; and entering from it into the unsetting darkness you receive, as the God-bearer did of old, letters traced by God, by which we are guided towards divine virtue and joyfully cry to you: rejoice, father Nilus, the adorning of fasters.

death.note: days.pravoslavie.ru's line for 12 ноября ст. ст. reads «Прп. Нила постника (V).», and azbyka.ru's line for the same day prints «(V)» as well. Its own life page sets his lifetime a century earlier — «жил в IV веке и был учеником святого Иоанна Златоуста» — which is not a contradiction but the other end of one life: a disciple of Chrysostom, who died in 407, who then spent forty years in a cave on Sinai reaches the fifth century. The century of the two calendar lines is taken for the death and the life's own sentence is recorded here. The folder carried no date at all before this reading, and neither doxologia.ro nor saint.gr gave one.
